tagline: Switchbacks climb from forest to alpine tundra on a seasonal Yellowstone approach.
intro: The Beartooth Highway climbs from forest to alpine tundra, with switchbacks carrying US 212 toward the Montana-Wyoming line. Designated an All-American Road in 2002, it offers views of snowcapped peaks, glaciers, alpine lakes and plateaus, as Visit Montana describes it. The Forest Service allows a minimum of two to three hours for the drive, with scenic pullouts and day hikes along the corridor.

Red Lodge was a coal town before it became a highway gateway: mining defined it until the 1930s, when the Depression forced many mines to close. Construction of the Beartooth Highway began in 1932, and the road was completed on June 14, 1936. The new highway linked Red Lodge with Yellowstone National Park. It remains a seasonal crossing, closed every winter by Montana’s transportation department.

Drive south from Red Lodge through Custer Gallatin National Forest, climbing past Vista Point’s view into the main canyon of Rock Creek. At the state line the road enters Shoshone National Forest, then reaches Beartooth Pass at 10,947 feet among lakes and pullouts. Near the top of the pass, the highway levels out onto a broad plateau. Westward, it descends to the Chief Joseph Scenic Byway junction and continues to Cooke City and Yellowstone’s northeast entrance.

moments.title: Vista Point
moments.text: Rock Creek’s main canyon is the feature to look for at Vista Point, on the climb south from Red Lodge. This is the Custer Gallatin National Forest portion of the road, where switchbacks take the highway toward the Wyoming line. Beyond that boundary, the route enters Shoshone National Forest and continues upward to Beartooth Pass.
moments.notice: Look into the main canyon of Rock Creek from Vista Point.

moments.title: Beartooth Basin Ski Area
moments.text: At Beartooth Basin, the road’s season shapes the ski season: US 212 closes in winter, and skiing is a summer activity. The ski area opened in 1962 in northern Wyoming’s Shoshone National Forest near the Montana border. Its 600 acres lie at an elevation of 10,900 feet. Two platter lifts serve the north-facing slopes, and there is no day lodge. Wikipedia describes it as North America’s only ski area open exclusively in summer, a distinction tied to the highway’s winter closure. The highway passes slightly above the summit of the ski area.

moments.title: Cooke City
moments.text: US 212 runs through the center of Cooke City, then leads southwest into Yellowstone National Park. The community takes its name from Jay Cooke, financier of the Northern Pacific Railroad. Tourism is its chief industry, including skiing and snowmobiling in winter. The eastern approach crosses 8,040-foot Colter Pass before US 212 reaches the center of the community. Cooke City and neighboring Silver Gate occupy the valley of Soda Butte Creek. That creek flows southwest into Wyoming to join the Lamar River inside Yellowstone, placing this end of the drive in the Yellowstone River watershed.

practical: Beartooth Basin Ski Area: The Forest Service lists the highway season as Memorial Day to October 15, weather dependent; check conditions near those dates. (checked 2026-10-11)
